rules: Sources import as 'Awaiting source verification'; no legal determination is made.
Internal classification (Prohibited Territory) is unchanged and is not a legal determination.
Collection authorisation fields are left blank for the compliance lead to set.
No requirements are proposed; these are watch-list sources only.
coverage_gaps: Brazil: this is a licensing regime (Law 14.790/2023, SPA/MF), not a prohibition; the 'Prohibited Territory' label may be out of date and should be reviewed by the compliance lead. Only the law text and SPA page are listed; individual SPA ordinances (e.g. 827/2024, 722/2024) were seen only on secondary sites, and the DOU URL was not confirmed.

India: Act and consolidated text now listed. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules 2026 (G.S.R. notification, 22 April 2026) and the Online Gaming Authority of India have no official URL seen yet; commencement date of 1 May 2026 comes from legal press, not the gazette.

Japan: Penal Code prohibition plus 2025 amendments to the gambling addiction countermeasures law (reported by law firms). The amended Basic Act on Countermeasures against Gambling Addiction (Act 74 of 2018; amendment promulgated 10 July 2025, in force 25 Sept 2025, per prefectural government pages) is on e-Gov, and the National Police Agency has an online-casino page, but I did not see their exact URLs, so none is listed.

Philippines: POGO ban (reported as RA 12312) and PAGCOR domestic e-gaming licensing. Search results confirm RA 12312 (Anti-POGO Act of 2025, signed 23 Oct 2025, per news reports) but no official PAGCOR or Official Gazette URL was seen, so none is listed. The Philippines has a licensed domestic online market, which may conflict with the 'Prohibited' label.

UAE: federal licensing via GCGRA now exists (reportedly effective 1 June 2026 per law-firm sources, unverified); the federal commercial gaming legislation is reported as not publicly available. The 'Prohibited' label may be out of date.

Australia: a trade site reports the Interactive Gambling Amendment (Gambling Reform) Bill 2026 passed on 19 August 2026; unverified and no official source seen. Federal Register of Legislation URL not confirmed.
Singapore: Gambling Control Act 2022 on Singapore Statutes Online was not opened directly; sso.agc.gov.sg is only mentioned by a GRA advisory.
Not yet researched: the other 69 Prohibited Territories.
